Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

peer noun

someone of the same age or standing

also peers, contemporary, people one’s own age, kids his own age, peer group, equal (a person)

classical

Cic. Sen. 10: adulēscēns ita dīlēxī senem ut aequālem (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fin. 5.42

aequālis, aequālis m./f.

noun (an adjective used as one), third declension; with a genitive or a possessive

someone of the same age; a contemporary

Peers by age: aequālis meus, someone my age; aequālēs, children of one’s own age. As an adjective it means equal (see equal).

Other words

  • pār, paris m./f. — an equal, a match; one of the same rank

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 7: parēs … cum paribus facillimē congregantur (Lewis & Short)

    Peers by standing rather than age. Lewis & Short gives it, with aequālis as a synonym, for “equal in station or age”.

Examples

  • deinde aequālibus dēlectantur libenterque sē cum iīs congregant dantque sē ad lūdendum fābellārumque audītiōne dūcuntur

    then they enjoy children their own age, gladly join them, give themselves up to play, and are drawn by hearing storiesCic. Fin. 5.42

  • parēs vetere prōverbiō cum paribus facillimē congregantur

    equals, as the old proverb says, flock together most easilyCic. Sen. 7 (Lewis & Short)

See also equal, friend.
